items.title: What Should This Section Be?
items.why:
Today it has a bloating score, five unlabeled symptom buttons (heartburn, cramps, gas, nausea, low energy) and an optional waist size. With no heading over the buttons, they're easy to miss, and only bloating feeds the pattern finder.

Team sports and strength coaches commonly use a short daily wellness questionnaire: fatigue or energy, sleep, muscle soreness, stress and mood, each on a small scale (Hooper and Mackinnon, 1995; McLean et al., 2010, which used 1 to 5). The Gymnastics check-in already asks these, so on a Gymnastics profile option A would show only the Stomach part.

options.label: A daily check-in, with the stomach questions folded under it
options.desc: Energy, sleep hours, muscle soreness, stress and mood, one tap each. Stomach ▾ holds bloating, the symptom buttons and waist.

options.label: Stomach only, finished properly
options.desc: A heading over the symptom buttons, headache added, and bowel movements in plain words (Goku's own: none, hard, normal, loose).

options.label: Remove the section
options.desc: The Symptom check-ins option and its pattern finder go away. Answers already saved stay in backups.

items.title: Which Questions
items.why: The pictures show my picks. Other ideas, if you want any: hunger, headache, motivation to train, and how your last workout felt. Say which to add or drop in the note.

options.label: As shown in the option you picked
Change them (say how in the note)

items.title: Let Patterns Use Every Answer
items.why: The pattern finder only looks at bloating now. It could look at every answer you keep: for example, foods that show up more on low-energy days, or poor sleep before high-soreness days. It would still wait for enough days before saying anything, and still say that showing up together isn't proof.

items.title: Out-of-Date Descriptions
items.why: Found while checking: the Symptom check-ins option says it covers “bloating, heartburn, cramps and energy”, and the Nutrition option still says “125,000 foods and 18 restaurant chains”. Goku now has 36 chains. Both would be rewritten to match what the app actually has after your picks.

items.title: What These Suggestions Might Have Wrong
items.why:
• The standard 7-type stool chart (the Bristol scale) is copyrighted, so option B uses Goku's own four plain words instead. They're less precise.
• I checked the two questionnaire papers' citations but haven't read their full text. Goku would use its own wording, not theirs, with the papers cited as where the idea comes from.
• On a Gymnastics profile, Symptom check-ins is off unless turned on, and option A doesn't repeat the readiness questions there.
• Patterns would show what lines up, not what causes it. More questions means more chance of a pattern that's only luck, so the finder would need the same minimum days for each answer.
